definition: A reaction in which a more reactive element takes the place of a less reactive one in a compound, releasing it. For example, chlorine displaces bromine from bromide ions.
An oxide, usually of a metal, that reacts with acids to form a salt and water. If it dissolves, it gives an alkaline solution, as sodium oxide does.
An oxide that reacts with both acids and bases to form salts. Aluminium oxide, $\ce{Al2O3}$, is the period 3 example.
An oxide, usually of a non-metal, that reacts with bases to form a salt and water. If it dissolves, it gives an acidic solution, as sulfur dioxide does.
Rain with a pH below about 5.6, made acidic by oxides of sulfur and nitrogen, mainly from burning fuels. Carbon dioxide alone only takes rain to about pH 5.6.
